title: NAT Configuration: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Now let's actually configure N A T. There are three ways to set it up. Static. Dynamic. And overload.

lines.t: Same idea, three ways to set it up

scenes.heading: The switchboard operator
scenes.narration: Think of a company switchboard. Two hundred staff share one public phone number, and each has a private extension. When extension two oh one calls out, the operator swaps in the company number, and notes it in a call log. When the customer calls back, she checks the log and connects them to the right extension. Outsiders never see the extensions, only the company number.

scenes.heading: Static or dynamic
scenes.narration: Here's how the first two differ. Static gives one fixed public address to one inside host. That's what you use for a server people connect to. Dynamic hands out addresses from a pool, and each host borrows one for a while.

scenes.heading: Overload in four steps
scenes.narration: The most common setup is overload, also called P A T. Mark the inside and outside interfaces. Write an access list for who may be translated. Then tie it to the outside interface with overload. And verify with show I P nat translations.

lines.t: ip nat inside / ip nat outside
ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/1 overload

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three things to remember. N A T hides addresses, but it isn't encryption or authentication. It can break protocols that hide addresses inside the data, like F T P. And translations time out, so entries disappear after a while.

items.right: It hides addresses; no encryption or authentication
FTP and others embed IPs and need help

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva NAT configuration lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Static is one to one, dynamic uses a pool, and overload shares one address. Mark the inside and outside interfaces first. And check your work with show I P nat translations. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva NAT configuration lab.
